02 | Privacy Policy
https://classcompanion.com/privacy
Webpage text snapshot | Retrieved 10 October 2026
Privacy Policy
This Privacy Policy describes how Class Companion, Inc. (“Class Companion,” “us,” “we,” and “our”) handles teacher
and student personal information that we collect through our website, https://classcompanion.com, and the Class
Companion platform (collectively, the “Service” or “Services”).
Class Companion respects and supports all applicable student data privacy laws. In that regard, we support schools in
complying with the Family Education Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA), and we comply with the Children's Online Privacy
Protection Act (COPPA). For specific questions, please contact [email protected].
‍
Privacy principles
We will not collect, maintain, use or share teacher and student personal information beyond that needed for authorized
educational/school purposes, or as authorized by the parent/student. We adhere to the NIST Cybersecurity Framework
("NIST CSF").
We promise to:
Collect only the minimum personal information necessary to provide our Services
Not sell your personal information to third parties
Not use your personal information for advertising
Enable you to control the personal information you provide to us
Protect your personal information
‍
Teacher information
We collect the minimal amount of information needed from teachers to deliver our Services. This information includes:
Account information, including first name, email address, school name. Last name is optional.
Content, such as your conversations with the AI chatbot, your written assignments, and other information you submit
through the platform or that is associated with your engagement with the Services.
Customer support requests, such as when you contact us with questions or feedback that does not contain teacher or
student personal information. ‍
Testimonials, if you choose to give us a testimonial about your experience with the Services. With your permission, we
may post your testimonial and related information publicly on the Services. To request the removal of your testimonial,
please contact [email protected].
This information is protected by our rigorous data privacy protocols consistent with industry standards.
‍
Information we obtain from third parties
Integrated technologies, such as Google Login or Clever. Only if you choose to use these integrated technologies will we
receive information such as your name and email address.
‍

name: Class Companion
text:
Automatic data collection
‍We and our service providers may automatically log information about you, your computer or mobile device, and your
interactions over time with our Services, our communications, and other online services, such as:
Device data, such as your computer’s or mobile device’s operating system type and version, manufacturer and model,
browser type, screen resolution, device type (e.g., phone, tablet), IP address, unique identifiers, language settings,
mobile device carrier, radio/network information (e.g., WiFi, LTE, 4G), and general location information such as city,
state or geographic area. We do not collect your exact geolocation.
Online activity data, such as pages or screens you viewed, how long you spent on a page or screen, navigation paths
between pages or screens, information about your activity on a page or screen, access times, duration of access, and
whether you have opened our emails or clicked links within them.
‍
We use the following tools for automatic data collection
Cookies, which are text files that websites store on a visitor‘s device to identify the visitor’s browser or to store
information or settings in the browser for the purpose of helping the visitor navigate between pages efficiently,
remembering preferences, enabling functionality, and helping us understand user activity and patterns. You can adjust
your web browser’s settings to refuse cookies.
Web beacons, also known as pixel tags or clear GIFs, which are used to demonstrate that a webpage or email was
accessed or opened, or that certain content was viewed or clicked.
‍
Student information
We collect the minimal amount of student information needed to deliver our Services. This typically includes:
Email address, so the student can login. We alter the email address to protect student privacy. We never contact
students for marketing purposes.
First name, so that the teacher can see who submitted which submission.
Content, which is the student’s submission to an assignment created by their teacher.
This information is protected by our rigorous data privacy protocols consistent with industry standards.
‍
How we use your personal information
We do not rent, sell, or exchange teacher or student personal information to any third party. We do not advertise using
teacher or student personal information. We do not build personal profiles of students other than for supporting
authorized educational/school purposes or as authorized by a school or school district.
‍
To provide our Services
Provide, operate, maintain, secure, and improve our Services.
Provide you with customer service, and respond to your requests and feedback.
Communicate with you about our Services, including by sending you announcements, updates, security alerts, and
support and administrative messages.
Understand your needs and interests, and personalize your experience with our Services and our communications.
‍

name: Class Companion
text:
Research and development
‍We first turn teacher and student personal information into anonymous data by removing information that makes the
data personally identifiable to you. Then, we use this de-identify data for research and development purposes. The goal
of research and development is to improve our Services. We may further aggregate the de-identified information. We
may use de-identified data and share it with third parties for our lawful business purposes. We only share data with third
parties that adhere to our policies, our contractural obligations, and applicable law and pledge to protect student privacy.
‍
For compliance and protection
Comply with applicable laws, lawful requests, and legal process, such as to respond to subpoenas or requests from
government authorities.
Protect our, your or others’ rights, privacy, safety, or property (including by making and defending legal claims).
Audit our internal processes for compliance with legal and contractual requirements and internal policies.
Enforce the terms and conditions that govern our Services.
Prevent, identify, investigate and deter fraudulent, harmful, unauthorized, unethical or illegal activity, including
cyberattacks and identity theft.
‍
How we share your personal information
We do not rent, sell, or exchange teacher or student personal information to any third party or use such personal
information for advertising purposes.
Data that you ask us to share. For users who belong to the same educational institution, we share personal information,
that you ask us to share, with other authorized users of the Services. For example, teachers can view their own students’
completed assignments and conversations through the AI chatbot.
Approved service providers. We hold approved service providers to the same rigorous privacy and security requirements
as ourselves. We only share information with third-party companies if it is necessary to deliver our Services (such as
cloud hosting, database management, and email delivery) and if the third party company adheres to our policies and
pledges to protect student privacy. We do not share teacher or student personally identifiable information with AI service
providers. Google Workspace APIs are not used to develop, improve, or train generalized AI and/or ML models. A list of
our third-party service providers can be found here.
Government authorities. We may be required to disclose teacher or student personal information to law enforcement,
government authorities, or private parties in order to comply with the law or a valid legal request.
Business transfers. In the event of an acquisition, merger, or reorganization or sale of assets, or in the event of
bankruptcy or dissolution, we will require the acquiring company to act in accordance with this Privacy Policy or allow
users a choice to send information to the future entity or have their information deleted.
‍
Your choices
Access, update, or delete your account information. You may access or update your personal information in your
account by logging in and editing your information. Parents may inspect and correct information for students. Schools
and districts may access, update, or delete student data maintained by the school or district. You can request that we
delete your account by emailing us at [email protected]. We may retain de-identified data after you delete your account,
in order to improve the operation of our Services; this data will not contain your personal information.
Opt out of emails. You may opt out of product update emails by following the opt-out or unsubscribe instructions at the
bottom of the email. You may continue to receive critical Service-related emails.
Online tracking opt out. There are a number of ways to limit online tracking, which we have summarized below:

name: Class Companion
text:
Blocking cookies in your browser. Most browsers let you remove or reject cookies. To do this, follow the instructions in
your browser settings. Many browsers accept cookies by default until you change your settings. For more information
about cookies, including how to see what cookies have been set on your device and how to manage and delete them,
visit www.allaboutcookies.org.
Using privacy plug-ins or browsers. You can block our services from setting cookies by using a browser with privacy
features, like Brave, or installing browser plugins like Privacy Badger, DuckDuckGo, Ghostery or uBlock Origin, and
configuring them to block third party cookies/trackers.
Note that because these opt-out mechanisms are specific to the device or browser on which they are exercised, you will
need to opt out on every browser and device that you use.
Do Not Track. Some Internet browsers may be configured to send “Do Not Track” signals to the online services that you
visit. We currently do not respond to “Do Not Track” or similar signals. To find out more about “Do Not Track,” please
visit https://www.allaboutdnt.com.
‍
Data retention
We retain your information to deliver our Service, but we do not retain it longer than necessary to support the authorized
educational/school purposes, or as authorized by the user.
You can deactivate your account by going to your account settings. When you deactivate an account, you will not be
able to access it, there will be no further activity in your account, and other users will no longer see any information
connected to your account. For students and teachers, this means your school will no longer be able to access
information connected to your account. You may restore the account by contacting [email protected].
When you deactivate your account, we turn personal information into anonymous data by removing information that
makes the data personally identifiable to you. We retain this de-identified data to improve our product. You may contact
us if you would like your data to be permanently deleted.
In the case of school contracts, the school may request that we deactivate and de-identify accounts, and we will do so,
unless there is a regulatory or valid legal need to retain certain information.
‍
Privacy Protection & Security
Protecting your privacy and security is important to us. We adhere to the NIST Cybersecurity Framework ("NIST CSF").
We use strict user access controls, multi-factor authentication, and a combination of technical and procedural
safeguards to protect your data. We secure data in transit and at rest using encryption. We have an incident response
plan in place and a break notification protocol.
Please note that any information you send to us electronically, while using the Services or otherwise interacting with us,
may not be secure when it is transmitted to us. Do not use unsecure channels to communicate sensitive or confidential
information to us.
‍
International visitors
If you use our Service outside of the United States, your data is collected in the country where you are located and then
transferred to the United States where our servers are located.
If you are located within the European Union (EU), European Economic Area (EEA), or the United Kingdom (UK), you
are afforded specific rights under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) or the UK GDPR. These rights include
the ability to access, rectify, erase, limit the processing of, or oppose the processing of your personal data. Should you
wish to exercise any of these rights, please contact [email protected].
Furthermore, as an EU/EEA or UK resident, you possess the right to file a complaint with your local data protection
authority regarding our handling of your personal information.
‍

text:

03 | Security
https://classcompanion.com/security
Webpage text snapshot | Retrieved 10 October 2026
Security Best Practices
We take the security of your data very seriously at Class Companion. We aim to be as clear and open as we can about
the way we handle security.
As much of our security measures are proprietary, if you have additional questions regarding security, we are happy to
answer them. Please write to [email protected] and we will respond as quickly as we can.
‍
Confidentiality
The operation of the Class Companion services requires that some employees have access to the systems which store
and process Customer Data. We place strict controls over our employees’ access to the data you and your users make
available via the Class Companion services ("Customer Data"), as more specifically defined in your agreement with
Class Companion covering the use of the Class Companion service, and are committed to ensuring that Customer Data
is not seen by anyone who should not have access to it.
Our employees are prohibited from using permissions to view Customer Data unless it is necessary to do so to provide
the Services. We have technical controls and audit policies in place to ensure that any access to Customer Data is
logged. All of our employees and contract personnel, if any, are bound to our policies regarding Customer Data and we
treat these issues as matters of the highest importance within our company.
‍
Compliance
The following security-related audits and certifications are applicable to the Class Companion services:
The environment that hosts the Class Companion services maintains multiple certifications for its data centers, including
ISO 27001 compliance, PCI Certification, and SOC attestations. For more information about their certification and
compliance, please visit the Render Trust and Security website.
‍
Data Encryption In Transit and At Rest
The Class Companion services support the latest recommended secure cipher suites and protocols to encrypt all traffic
in transit. Customer Data is encrypted at rest.
We monitor the changing cryptographic landscape closely and work promptly to upgrade the service to respond to new
cryptographic weaknesses as they are discovered and implement best practices as they evolve. For encryption in
transit, we do this while also balancing the need for compatibility for legacy clients.
‍
Availability
We understand that you rely on the Class Companion services to work. We’re committed to making Class Companion a
highly-available service that you can count on. Our infrastructure runs on systems that are fault tolerant, for failures of
individual servers or even entire data centers. Our operations team tests disaster-recovery measures regularly and staffs
an around-the-clock on-call team to quickly resolve unexpected incidents.
‍

name: Class Companion
text:
Disaster Recovery
Customer Data is stored redundantly at multiple locations in our hosting provider’s data centers to ensure availability.
We have well-tested backup and restoration procedures, which allow recovery from a major disaster. Customer Data
and our source code are automatically backed up nightly. The Operations team is alerted in case of a failure with this
system.
‍
Network Protection
In addition to sophisticated system monitoring and logging, we have implemented IP allowlisted authentication for all
server access across our production environment. Firewalls are configured according to industry best practices and
unnecessary ports are blocked by configuration with AWS Security Groups.
‍
Logging
Class Companion maintains an extensive, centralized logging environment in its production environment which contains
information pertaining to security, monitoring, availability, access, and other metrics about the Class Companion
services. These logs are analyzed for security events via automated monitoring software, overseen by the security team.
‍
Incident Management & Response
In the event of a security breach, Class Companion will promptly notify you of any unauthorized access to your
Customer Data. Class Companion has incident management policies and procedures in place to handle such an event.
‍
External Security Audits
We continuously automated security compliance using Vanta security monitoring which performs regular audits of Class
Companion services. We also conduct self assessments on a bi-annual basis. In addition to continuous audits of Class
Companion services and features, we also employ the use of continuous hybrid automated scanning of our web
platform.
‍
Product Security Practices
New features, functionality, and design changes go through a security review process facilitated by the security team. In
addition, our code is audited with automated static analysis software, tested, and manually peer-reviewed prior to being
deployed to production. The security team works closely with development teams to resolve any additional security
concerns that may arise during development.
If you find a vulnerability in the Class Companion product, please reach out to [email protected].
‍
Last Updated: 22nd April, 2025

2. How We Use Your Information
We use the collected information for various purposes:
Provide Services: To deliver, maintain, and improve our AI-powered assessment platform
Process Exams: To generate questions, grade submissions, and provide analytics
Communication: To send you updates, newsletters, and support messages

Personalization: To customize your experience and recommend features
Analytics: To understand usage patterns and improve our service

Compliance: To comply with legal obligations and enforce our terms

Encryption: All data is encrypted in transit (TLS/SSL) and at rest
Access Controls: Role-based access and authentication requirements
Secure Infrastructure: Hosted on secure, SOC 2 compliant servers (Supabase)
Regular Audits: Security assessments and vulnerability testing
Data Backups: Regular automated backups with encryption
Limited Retention: Data is retained only as long as necessary
Important: While we strive to protect your information, no method of transmission over the internet or electronic storage
is 100% secure. We cannot guarantee absolute security.

Supabase (Database & Authentication)
Stores user accounts, exam data, and application information. Supabase is SOC 2 Type II certified and GDPR
compliant.

Your institution's data,

Every institution runs in a dedicated, isolated workspace (separate database schema and subdomain). One school can

Data is encrypted in transit with TLS and encrypted at rest by default on Google Cloud — covering answer sheets,
scores, and student records.

Granular roles (admin, teacher, student, parent) ensure users see only what they should. Administrator and platform
accounts are protected with multi-factor authentication.

results and is not used to train external AI models.

Hosted on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) with managed, industry-standard infrastructure. Payments run on Cashfree's
hosted checkout — we never store card details.

Platform actions are logged for traceability. Any support access is controlled and recorded, giving institutions clear
accountability.

Collection
We collect only what's needed for evaluation — answer sheets, question papers, rubrics, scores, and student identifiers

In transit
All data moves over encrypted TLS connections.

Webpage text snapshot | Retrieved 10 October 2026
Frizzle, Inc (“Frizzle,” “we,” “us”) provides an AI assessment and instructional-analytics service for schools and
educators (the “Service”). This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, share, and protect personal information,
including student data schools upload.
This is our public privacy notice and public student-data terms. It is incorporated into our Terms of Service. It is not a
substitute for a signed Data Privacy Agreement. Schools and districts can request a signed DPA at support@frizzle.com.
If you have a signed DPA, order form, or MSA with us, that document controls if it conflicts with this Policy.
We process student data as a school official under FERPA, only for the school, and only for the educational purposes
the school authorized. The school (not Frizzle) owns and controls student data. Parents and eligible students exercise
FERPA rights through the school.
The Service is for authorized educators and school staff. Students do not create accounts or log in.
1. Who this covers
Educators and school staff who create accounts (including individual teacher plans).
Schools and districts that buy or authorize the Service.
Students, only as data the school or a teacher uploads (assignment images, names or identifiers the teacher includes,
scores). We do not collect information directly from students.
If you are a parent, contact your school. We cannot verify parental identity against a school’s records from this website.
2. Information we collect
Educator and account information
Name, email, profile image (if you use Google Sign-In)
School or district affiliation you provide
Authentication data (password hashes or SSO tokens)
Role (teacher, admin) and account settings
Billing details for teacher plans (processed by Stripe; we do not store full card numbers)
Support emails and feedback
Student information (uploaded by the school or teacher)
Images or scans of student work (handwriting, worksheets, quizzes)
Student names, roster identifiers, class/section, grade level, if the teacher adds them
Scores, flags, comments, misconception tags, and other Output we generate
Optional assignment titles, standards, or rubric text the teacher enters
We do not need, and you should not upload, student home addresses, Social Security numbers, health records, or
similar sensitive data that is not required to assess the work.
Usage, device, and diagnostics
Log data (IP address, browser, timestamps, pages or features used)
Approximate location derived from IP
Cookies and similar tech on our sites (see §8)
Product analytics to see which features work

name: Frizzle
text:
Security and abuse logs (see §9)
Information from integrations
If you connect Google Sign-In or a later LMS/SSO (for example Google Classroom), we receive only what that provider
sends for login and the scopes you authorize. See §7.
We do not have to collect every item above for every user.
3. How we use information
We use personal information to:
Provide the Service: authenticate you, assess and analyze uploaded work, show results to the teacher or school that
submitted them
Operate, secure, and debug the Service, including detecting Prompt Injection, Prompt Extraction, Model Extraction,
fraud, ineligible (including competitor) use, and other abuse, as described in the Terms
Bill teacher plans and school invoices, and prevent payment fraud
Provide support and service-related notices (including auto-renewal reminders)
Comply with law and with school instructions
Create de-identified or aggregated insights that cannot reasonably identify a student, educator, or school
Student work and other Customer Data are not used to train Frizzle’s foundation models, and our model providers are
contractually prohibited from using that data to train their models. “Improve the Service” in this Policy means product
reliability, security, and support.
4. How AI processing works
The Service uses AI, including third-party models, to read student work and produce scores, flags, and comments.
Input (the image or text you submit, plus limited context such as the problem or rubric) is sent to our systems and, as
needed, to AI subprocessors listed on our subprocessor page.
Those providers process Input to return Output to Frizzle for you. They are under contract not to train on that data and
not to use it for their own purposes. We require zero-retention from all providers.
We do not use student data for advertising, profiling for ads, or sale.
Output can be wrong. Teachers must review it. We do not make autonomous high-stakes decisions about students
(placement, discipline, report cards) without a human in the loop.
5. What we do not do
Sell personal information
Share personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising (CCPA/CPRA “sharing”)
Use student data to market to students or families
Allow students to create accounts
Train foundation models on student work or educator content
Let subprocessors use Frizzle data for their own ML, ads, or product training
6. When we share information
We share personal information only:
With the school that owns the tenancy (admins can see their teachers’ use and Customer Data)
With subprocessors who help us run the Service, under contract, listed at frizzle.com/legal/subprocessors. We will
update that page when the list changes and, for student data, follow any notice period in a signed DPA.

name: Frizzle
text:
If you ask us to, or the school instructs us to
For legal reasons: to comply with law or valid legal process; to protect students, schools, or Frizzle; to enforce the Terms
(including shutting off injection, extraction, or ineligible company use)
In a merger or sale of Frizzle, with the buyer bound to continue protecting the data as this Policy (or the signed DPA)
requires. We will not treat a sale of the company as a sale of student personal information under SOPPA-style rules.
We do not sell student information. We do not disclose student information except as the school directs or as this Policy /
a DPA / law allows.
7. Google Sign-In
If you log in with Google, we receive basic profile information (name, email, profile image) for authentication and account
administration. We do not request Classroom, Drive, Gmail, contacts, or Calendar unless we later add an integration you
separately authorize.
Frizzle’s use and transfer of information received from Google APIs will adhere to the Google API Services User Data
Policy, including the Limited Use requirements. We do not use Google user data for advertising. You can disconnect
Google in account settings or through your Google account.
8. Cookies, analytics, and the marketing site
We use cookies and similar storage to keep you logged in, remember preferences, and measure use of the product and
marketing site. We do not use student data for advertising cookies.
You can block cookies in your browser; the Service may not function fully without essential cookies.
9. Security, monitoring, and retention
We use encryption in transit and at rest, access controls, authentication, logging, and vendor contracts.
We may monitor Input, Output, images, and metadata to operate and secure the Service and to detect abuse, as
described in the Terms. That monitoring is for security and enforcement.
Retention. Educator account data is kept while the account is open and for a reasonable period afterward for billing,
security, and legal records.
Student data is kept only as long as needed to provide the Service to that school, or as the school instructs. On contract
or account termination, or earlier on school request, we delete or return Customer Data from production systems within
sixty (60) days (backups in the ordinary cycle, longer if a legal hold applies), unless a signed DPA sets a different
timeline.
10. Security incidents
If we discover a breach of personal information, we will notify the affected school without unreasonable delay and within
legally required timelines, including as required by FERPA guidance, state student-privacy laws, and NY Education Law
2-d (notification to the educational agency no later than 7 calendar days after discovery, where that law applies). We will
not notify parents directly unless the school or law requires us to; the school is the point of contact for families.
11. FERPA, COPPA, SOPPA, NY 2-d, SDPC
FERPA. We act as a school official with a legitimate educational interest. We use student data only for authorized
educational purposes, under the school’s direction. We do not redisclose except as the school directs or FERPA allows.
COPPA. Students cannot create accounts. We do not knowingly collect personal information directly from children under
13. The school is the consenting authority for student data it uploads (COPPA school-consent).
SOPPA, NY Ed Law 2-d, SDPC. We support school compliance: no sale of student data, no targeted ads to students,
subprocessors under contract, deletion on request, breach notice, and a signed DPA on request. A Parents’ Bill of
Rights-style summary: the school owns the data; Frizzle does not sell it; parents should go to the school to inspect or
correct education records.

support@frizzle.com or using in-product admin tools.
Educators may access and update account information in settings, disconnect Google, cancel a teacher plan as

The Service is not directed at children. Students must not create accounts. If we learn a student has created an account,

We may update this Policy. We will change the “Last updated” date and, for material changes, notify the primary email

Legal
Privacy Policy
Last updated 17 April 2025
Information We Collect
When you create an account or use MarkBot, we collect:
Account data — your name and email address.
Uploaded content — exam papers and any marking rubrics you provide.
Payment data — billing details, processed securely by Stripe. We never store card numbers.
Usage data — pages marked, credit balance, session logs.
How We Use It
We use your information only to operate and improve the service:
Process your exam papers through AI and return results.
Manage your account, credits, and payment history.
Send transactional emails (marking complete, low credits, etc.).
Diagnose technical issues and improve accuracy.
We do not sell your data. We do not use your papers to train models.
Data Storage & Security
Uploaded exam papers are stored in Supabase (EU region) and are tied to your account. You can delete them at any
time. Marking results are retained until you delete them or close your account.
All data in transit is encrypted with TLS. Stored files are encrypted at rest. Access is restricted by row-level security —
only you can read your papers.
Third-Party Services
We share data with the following processors, and only to the extent needed:
Google Gemini — receives paper images/text to perform marking. Google's enterprise API terms prohibit training on
submitted data.
Stripe — handles payment processing. We pass your billing info; we never store it ourselves.
Supabase — provides database and file storage. Data is hosted in the EU.
Your Rights
You can, at any time:
Export all your data from your account settings.
Delete individual papers or full marking batches.
Close your account and have all data permanently erased.
Contact us to correct any inaccurate personal information.

Cookies

third-party analytics scripts are loaded.
Contact

Legal
Terms of Service
Last updated 17 April 2025
Acceptance of Terms
By creating an account or using MarkBot you agree to these Terms of Service. If you do not agree, do not use the
service.
What MarkBot Does
MarkBot uses AI (Google Gemini) to analyse and grade student exam papers against provided or inferred marking
criteria. Results are returned to the teacher who submitted the papers.
MarkBot is a tool to assist teachers — not a replacement for professional judgement. Final grading decisions remain with
the teacher.
Your Responsibilities
By using MarkBot you agree to:
Provide accurate account information and keep credentials secure.
Only upload content you have the right to process (e.g. papers from your own classes).
Not use the service for any unlawful purpose.
Review AI-generated marks before sharing results with students.
Comply with any data protection obligations applicable to you (e.g. GDPR, UK GDPR).
Credits & Payment
MarkBot operates on a prepaid credit system:
1 credit = 1 page of marking.
Credits are deducted when a batch is submitted. If a batch fails, credits are automatically refunded.
Credits do not expire.
All purchases are final. Credits cannot be exchanged for cash.
Payments are processed by Stripe. Your card details are handled by Stripe and never stored by us.
AI Limitations & Accuracy
AI marking is not perfect. Factors like poor scan quality, ambiguous handwriting, or unusual question formats can affect
accuracy.
Always review AI output before returning results to students.
Do not rely solely on MarkBot for high-stakes or formal assessments.
MarkBot is not liable for marks that are later found to be incorrect.

Privacy Policy
Version 2.0 · Effective date 15 September 2026
Introduction
This Privacy Policy explains how Top Marks AI Ltd ("Top Marks", "we", "us") collects and uses personal data when you
visit our website, contact us, or use the Top Marks platform (the "Platform"), our AI-assisted marking and feedback
service for schools.
We act in two roles. For student assessment data and staff accounts on the Platform, the school is the controller and we
act as its processor under Schedule 1 (Data Processing Agreement) to our Platform Terms and Conditions
(topmarks.ai/terms). For our website, enquiries, marketing and business contacts, we are the controller. This Policy is a
notice describing our processing; it does not form part of, and does not vary, our contract with any school.
We comply with the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR), the Data Protection Act 2018 and, where
applicable, the EU GDPR. We review this Policy regularly; the date of the last update is shown above. Questions may be
sent to the contact details in section 13.
1. What Data Do We Collect About You?
Personal data is information that relates to you and identifies you, or can be used to identify you, such as your name,
email address or digital identifiers such as IP addresses.
1.1 Data we process on behalf of schools (as processor)
Schools provide this data directly (for example, by upload or manual entry) or authorise us to retrieve it from their
Management Information System (MIS) through Wonde's API. It comprises:
Student Data: full name or student identification number; year group and class (where the school provides them); exam
or essay responses, including handwritten responses converted into text; and assessment results and feedback
generated by the Platform.
Staff Data: full name; email address; institution name; hashed login credentials; records linking uploaded assessments
to teacher accounts; and support communications with us.
1.2 Data we collect as controller
Website and Platform usage data: IP address, browser type, operating system, pages visited, features used and time
spent, collected through server logs, cookies and similar technologies (see section 11 and our Cookie Policy at
topmarks.ai/cookies).
Enquiry and business contact data: name, role, organisation, contact details and the content of our correspondence with
prospective and existing school customers, partners and suppliers.
Marketing preferences: your consent or opt-out status for marketing communications.
We do not require or deliberately collect special category data, such as health information or biometric data. Free-text
assessment responses may occasionally contain such information; it is processed only as part of the assessment
content and is never used for profiling.
We may aggregate and anonymise personal data to produce statistical data (for example, the percentage of users who
use a particular Platform feature). Aggregated data does not identify you and is not personal data. If we ever re-combine
it with personal data, we treat the combined data as personal data under this Policy.
2. How Do We Collect Your Personal Data?
We collect your data in the following ways:

Directly from you, when you sign up, contact us or use the Platform.
From schools, which provide student and staff data for assessment purposes, either directly (for example, by CSV
upload or manual entry) or from the school's MIS via Wonde's API, at the instruction of an authorised school
administrator when the integration is configured. The school specifies which categories of data are retrieved and can
disable the integration at any time.
Automatically, through cookies and similar technologies when you interact with our website or the Platform.
3. How Do We Use Your Personal Data?
For student assessment data and staff Platform accounts, we act as processor on the school's documented instructions.
The school determines the purposes and the lawful basis (for most schools, public task under Article 6(1)(e) UK GDPR;
for independent schools, typically contract or legitimate interests). Neither we nor the school rely on consent for this
processing. Our processing on behalf of schools is described in Annex A to Schedule 1 of our Platform Terms and
Conditions and in our DPIA Support Pack.
Where we act as controller, we process personal data for the following purposes:
What we use your Personal Data for | What Personal Data we collect | Our lawful basis for processing |
To respond to enquiries and manage our relationship with schools, prospective customers, partners and suppliers |
Enquiry and business contact data | Legitimate interests (running and developing our business); performance of a
contract, where you are our customer |
To operate, secure and improve our website and the Platform, and to prevent fraud and misuse | Usage data, device
information, IP address, login activity | Legitimate interests (security and service improvement) |
To send marketing communications about our services | Contact details, marketing preferences | Consent, or legitimate
interests where the 'soft opt-in' applies (see section 11) |
To comply with legal obligations, such as accounting and regulatory requirements | Any necessary personal data |
Compliance with a legal obligation |
4. Do We Share Your Personal Data?
We do not sell or rent personal data. We share it only as follows:
With our service providers, which process it on our behalf and on our instructions: the hosting, database, file storage,
analytics and email delivery providers for the Platform (listed, with locations, at topmarks.ai/subprocessors), and the
business tools we use as controller, such as our CRM, support and email systems. We do not allow service providers to
use your personal data for their own purposes.
With the school, which as controller has access through the Platform to its own students' and staff's data. This is the
controller's own access rather than a disclosure by us.
With AI model providers, but only anonymised assessment content from which student identity and incidental identifiers
have been removed. No personal data is shared with them.
Where required by law, a court order or a regulator.
5. Children's Privacy
Where a school in the UK or the EEA uses the Platform, it does so as an educational institution in the course of providing
education to its pupils. In that context:
Consent is not the lawful basis. Neither we nor the school rely on consent under Article 6(1)(a) UK GDPR (or EU GDPR)
for the processing of student assessment data. The school identifies and maintains its own lawful basis for sharing that
data with us, and confirms that it has done so when it signs its Subscription Contract or Trial Agreement. Parental or
guardian consent is therefore not generally required before a UK or EEA school shares student data with us for
assessment purposes.
Privacy notices are provided by the school. Because the school is the controller and we have no direct relationship with
students or their families, the school is responsible for providing the information required by Articles 13 and 14 to
students and, where appropriate, their parents or guardians. We publish this Privacy Policy and our DPIA Support Pack

name: Top Marks AI
text:
to help schools do this.
Limited data collection. We process only the student data the school chooses to provide, and only to the extent
necessary to deliver automated marking and feedback. We do not collect student email addresses or contact students
directly.
6. How Do We Protect Your Data?
Personal data is encrypted in transit using TLS and at rest using AES-256 encryption. Access to personal data is
restricted by role to staff who need it, protected by multi-factor authentication, and logged. Student and staff data
processed on behalf of schools is hosted in the United Kingdom and the European Union. Top Marks holds Cyber
Essentials certification. Further detail on our security measures is set out in our DPIA Support Pack.
Where we have given you (or you have chosen) a password, you are responsible for keeping it confidential. Please do
not share your password with anyone.
7. How Long Do We Keep Your Data?
We keep personal data only for as long as reasonably necessary for the purposes described in this Policy and to comply
with our legal obligations:
Student assessment data and staff Platform accounts are held on behalf of schools as their processor. We do not delete
this data on our own initiative. It is retained for the school's Licence Period and then returned or deleted in accordance
with paragraph 11 of Schedule 1 to our Platform Terms and Conditions (deletion within 90 days of the end of the
contract, or within 30 days of the school's instruction, after the school's 60-day export period), or earlier on the school's
instruction.
Enquiry records and business contact data held as controller are deleted 24 months after our last contact with you, after
notifying you first.
Website and Platform usage data is retained for the periods set out in our Cookie Policy and, for security logs, for 12
months.
Some data may be retained for longer where required by law, for example accounting records.
8. International Data Transfers
Student and staff data that we process on behalf of schools is stored and processed in the United Kingdom and the
European Economic Area (EEA). Anonymised assessment content is sent to AI model providers in the United States; it
does not identify any individual and is not personal data.
Some of the business tools we use as controller, such as CRM, support, email and analytics systems, may store enquiry
and business contact data outside the UK and EEA, including in the United States. Where we transfer personal data
outside the UK or EEA, we rely on UK adequacy regulations or an EU adequacy decision, or we put in place the UK
International Data Transfer Agreement or Addendum (for transfers from the UK) or the EU Standard Contractual
Clauses (for transfers from the EEA). You can ask us for more detail about the safeguards used by contacting us
(section 13).
A current list of our sub-processors, by name and location, is at topmarks.ai/subprocessors.
9. Automated Decision-Making
The Platform uses artificial intelligence to generate suggested grades and written feedback on student work. These
suggestions are reviewed by the school's teaching staff, who retain final judgement; nothing is released to a student or
used for any summative or reporting purpose without that review. We do not make any decision producing legal or
similarly significant effects on any individual solely by automated means.

10. Your Rights
Where we process your personal data on behalf of a school as its processor, which includes student assessment data
and staff Platform accounts, the school is the controller and decides how rights requests are handled. You may contact
the school directly, or contact us at info@topmarks.ai and we will acknowledge your request and refer it to your school
within two business days. Where we process personal data as controller in our own right (section 3), we handle your
request ourselves, normally within one month.
Under the UK GDPR and, where applicable, the EU GDPR, you have the following rights:
Access: to request a copy of your personal data.
Rectification: to have inaccurate or incomplete data corrected.
Erasure: to have your data deleted where there is no good reason for us to continue processing it.
Restriction: to limit our processing in certain circumstances.
Objection: to object to processing based on legitimate interests, and to direct marketing at any time.
Portability: to receive the data you have provided to us in a structured, machine-readable format.
Withdrawal of consent: where processing is based on consent, to withdraw it at any time.
Complaint: if you are unhappy with how we have handled your personal data, please contact our data protection lead
(COO) at info@topmarks.ai so that we can try to resolve the matter. You also have the right to complain to the
Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk, 0303 123 1113) or, in the EEA, to your local supervisory authority.
11. Marketing and Cookies
We may send you marketing communications about our services by email where you have consented or where the 'soft
opt-in' applies, that is, where you have enquired about or purchased our services and have not opted out. You can opt
out at any time by using the unsubscribe link in any marketing email or by contacting us (section 13). Opting out of
marketing does not affect service communications that we need to send you about the Platform or your account. We will
not share your personal data with any other organisation for its own marketing purposes.
Our website and the Platform use cookies and similar technologies for essential functions and, with your consent, for
analytics. Details of the cookies we use, their purposes and how to manage them are in our Cookie Policy at
topmarks.ai/cookies.
12. Updates to This Privacy Policy
We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will publish the updated version at topmarks.ai/privacy with a
new 'last updated' date and, for significant changes, notify Platform users by email or by a notice on the Platform.
13. Contact Us
For any questions about this Privacy Policy or to exercise your rights, please contact us:
Email: info@topmarks.ai
Address: Harben House, Harben Parade, Finchley Road, London, United Kingdom, NW3 6LH
ICO registration number:ZB903015
Data protection lead:Chief Operating Officer

Our Sub-processors
Version 2.0 · Effective date 15 September 2026
Top Marks AI Ltd ("Top Marks") uses the third-party providers listed below to deliver the Top Marks platform. This list is
maintained in accordance with paragraph 8 of Schedule 1 (Data Processing Agreement) to the Platform Terms and
Conditions (topmarks.ai/terms). Top Marks gives Customers at least 30 days' written notice before engaging a new
sub-processor to process Personal Data or materially changing an existing sub-processor's role, and records each
change in the change log in section 3.
1. Sub-processors that process Personal Data on behalf of Customers
The following providers process Personal Data (student and staff data) as Top Marks' sub-processors. All of this
processing takes place in the United Kingdom or the European Economic Area, so no international transfer safeguard is
required.
Sub-processor | Role | Personal Data processed | Hosting location |
Render | Application hosting for the Platform's web application and processing servers | All Customer Data processed by
the Platform | Frankfurt, Germany (EU) |
MongoDB (MongoDB Atlas, deployed on AWS) | Primary database and automated backups | All Customer Data stored
by the Platform | Ireland (EU) |
Amazon Web Services | Temporary storage of uploaded scripts and generated exports (Amazon S3); underlying
infrastructure for the MongoDB Atlas database;
and, for schools using the Exam Decoder service, hosting of the orchestration service that matches handwritten scripts
to student records | Uploaded assessment files, transcriptions and exports; for Exam Decoder schools, the data used to
match scripts to students | Ireland (EU) |
Google Cloud Platform | Compute infrastructure for Top Marks' self-managed OCR transcription service. In the standard
flow, scripts carry an anonymising QR code or barcode and are anonymised before transcription. For schools using the
Exam Decoder service, the OCR reads uploaded scripts that may contain personal data, such as a student's handwritten
name, so that scripts can be matched to student records | Uploaded scripts and their transcriptions; for Exam Decoder
schools, including student names written on scripts | London, United Kingdom |
Amplitude | Product analytics | Usage data and account identifiers of Authorised Users | EU data centre, Frankfurt,
Germany |
Brevo | Service and account email delivery to Authorised Users | Staff names and email addresses | France (EU) |
MIS integration (Wonde): Wonde is engaged by the school, not by Top Marks. The school's data manager authorises, in
Wonde's portal, which student and staff records Wonde makes available to Top Marks, and can withdraw that
authorisation at any time. Wonde therefore acts as the school's own processor and is not a Top Marks sub-processor; it
is mentioned here for transparency because it forms part of the data flow into the Platform.
2. Providers that receive anonymised assessment content only
The following providers receive assessment content only after student identity has been separated from it and incidental
identifiers have been removed (see paragraph 3.1(d) of Annex A to Schedule 1). They do not process Personal Data on
behalf of Customers and are listed for transparency. Each is engaged on business terms under which customer content
is not used to train the provider's models.

Portkey | AI gateway that routes anonymised content to the model providers below, with load balancing and failover |
United States |

Version 2.0 · Effective date 15 September 2026
These Terms and Conditions govern the Customer's use of the Top Marks Platform and the services provided by Top
Marks. By executing a Contract that incorporates these Terms and Conditions, the Customer agrees to be bound by
them. The individual signing a Contract on behalf of a school, trust or other legal entity confirms that they have authority

agree as follows:
1. Definitions and Interpretation
1.1 In this Agreement, the following definitions apply. Additional terms may be defined elsewhere in this Agreement.
“Affiliate” | means, in respect of a party, each and any subsidiary or holding company of that party and each and any

given in section 1159 of the Companies Act 2006); |
“Agreement” | means these Terms and Conditions, including the Schedules and Annexes to them, the SLA, and each
Contract agreed between the parties; |
“Applicable Law” | means any (a) legislation (including statute, statutory instrument, treaty, regulation, order, rules,
directive, by-law, decree), common law and regulatory requirements; and (b) mandatory directions, codes, guidelines,
and requirements of any regulator having legal effect; |
“Authorised Users” | means the individuals employed or engaged by Customer whom Customer nominates as
authorised to use the Platform; |
"Business Day" | means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in England and Wales, and has a

“Confidential Information” | means information that is proprietary or confidential and is either clearly labelled as such or

documentation relating to the Platform; |
“Contract” | means a Subscription Contract or a Trial Agreement; |
“Customer Data” | means Student Data, data relating to Authorised Users, and any other data that Customer or its

“Customer” | means the entity identified as the ‘Customer’ in a Contract; |
“Customer Branding” | means any Customer trademarks, trade names, service marks, trade dress and logos, and
identifying slogans and symbols, in each case whether or not registered; |
“Data Protection Legislation” | has the meaning given to it in paragraph 1 of Schedule 1; |
“Deprioritisation” | has the meaning given to it in clause 6.9; |
“Effective Date” | means the date set out as the ‘Effective Date’ in the Contract; |
"Fair Usage Policy" | means the fair usage policy set out in clauses 6.7 to 6.12, describing the measures Top Marks may
apply where Customer's usage of the Platform exceeds a Usage Threshold; |
“Fees” | means the fees payable by Customer to Top Marks under this Agreement, as set out in a Contract; |
"Hard Speed Cap" | means a technical restriction applied by Top Marks to the rate or volume of marking requests
processed for Customer, resulting in slower processing of Customer's marking requests than would otherwise apply; |

2.4 Authorised User access and roles:

(a) Top Marks shall make the Platform available to each Authorised User nominated by Customer. The functionality
available to an Authorised User is determined by the role assigned to them by Customer's administrator from the roles
Top Marks makes available from time to time.
(b) The roles available as at the Effective Date are:
(i) User — upload of assessment materials, submission of marking requests, and access to review, amend, moderate
and export Output in respect of assessments that Authorised User has uploaded or that have been shared with them by
another Authorised User; and
(ii) Administrator — all functionality available to a User under paragraph (i), together with (A) invitation, management and
removal of Authorised Users and assignment of their roles, (B) configuration of Customer's account settings, including
authentication settings, and (C) access to marking results and feedback in respect of assessments uploaded by any
Authorised User within Customer's account.
An Administrator's access under paragraph (ii)(C) is not limited to assessments that Administrator has uploaded or that
have been shared with them.
(c) Customer is responsible for assigning and periodically reviewing roles. Each account is personal to the individual
Authorised User, and credentials must not be shared.
2.5 Top Marks shall, during the Licence Period, provide bug-fixes and minor updates to the Platform to Customer at no
additional cost.
2.6 Top Marks may, during the Licence Period, develop and offer to Customer new and enhanced versions of the
Platform, with Fees to be agreed between the parties.
3. Customer Obligations
3.1Except to the extent expressly agreed by the parties, or to the extent Applicable Law prohibits such a restriction,
Customer shall not, and shall ensure that no Authorised User does:
a) copy, reproduce, modify, adapt, create derivative works of, publish, distribute, sell, provide access to or otherwise
commercially exploit any part of the Platform;
b) frame or mirror any part of the Platform;
c) reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to discover the source code, underlying ideas or
algorithms of any part of the Platform;
d) access or use the Platform to develop a competing product or service;
e) use the Platform, or permit any other person to use it, in any manner that breaches Applicable Law or infringes the
rights of any third party;
f) upload, post or transmit through the Platform any material that is unlawful, defamatory, obscene, harassing or
otherwise harmful, or that contains malicious code;
g) obscure, remove or delete any copyright or other proprietary notices from the Platform or Output;
h) use the Platform for any purpose reasonably likely to bring Top Marks into disrepute;
i) interfere or attempt to interfere with the integrity or security of the Platform; or
j) attempt to gain access to data of any other customer of Top Marks held on the Platform.
3.2 Customer shall:
a) not upload to the Platform confidential data belonging to a third party without that third party's consent;
b) not sell, rent, lease, sublicense, lend or otherwise make the Platform available to any person other than its Authorised

without undue delay and in any event within 2 Business Days of receipt, and shall acknowledge receipt to the requester
and confirm that the request has been referred to the Customer as controller. Where the Customer instructs Top Marks
to give effect to a request, Top Marks shall do so within 10 Business Days of receiving the Customer's documented
instruction, or sooner where the Customer notifies Top Marks that a shorter period is necessary to meet its own statutory
deadline; and
b) becoming aware of any personal data breach affecting Personal Data processed on the Customer's behalf, in which
case Top Marks shall notify the Customer without undue delay and in any event within 48 hours of becoming aware.

name: Top Marks AI
text:
Such notification shall describe the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate number of data subjects and
records concerned, the likely consequences, and the measures taken or proposed to address it. Where and to the extent
that it is not possible to provide all of that information at the same time, Top Marks shall provide it in phases without
further undue delay. Top Marks shall also provide reasonable assistance in relation to the Customer's obligations to
notify regulators, supervisory authorities and data subjects.
5. Data protection impact assessments
Top Marks shall provide reasonable assistance to the Customer with data protection impact assessments, and with any
related prior consultation with the Information Commissioner's Office or other supervisory authority, taking into account
the nature of the processing and the information available to Top Marks. Top Marks' DPIA Support Pack is provided free
of charge for this purpose. Where the Customer requests assistance that goes materially beyond the DPIA Support Pack
and the information described in paragraph 6, Top Marks may charge its reasonable costs, agreed with the Customer in
advance.
6. Assistance with security of processing
Top Marks shall provide reasonable assistance to the Customer in ensuring compliance with the Customer's obligations
under Article 32 of the Data Protection Legislation (security of processing), taking into account the nature of the
processing and the information available to Top Marks. Such assistance may include:
(a) providing the Customer, on written request, with information about the technical and organisational security
measures implemented by Top Marks in connection with the processing of Personal Data under this Agreement,
including details of encryption standards, access controls, authentication requirements and data segregation
arrangements;
(b) notifying the Customer promptly of any material change to Top Marks' technical and organisational security
measures which may reduce the level of protection afforded to the Personal Data;
(c) cooperating with reasonable security assessments or reviews conducted by or on behalf of the Customer, subject to
the audit rights and limitations set out in paragraph 10; and
(d) providing such information as the Customer may reasonably require to enable the Customer to assess the risks
associated with the processing and to implement appropriate complementary security measures on its own systems.
The scope of assistance provided under this paragraph 6 is limited to information and activities within Top Marks'
reasonable knowledge and control, and is subject to the Customer reimbursing Top Marks' reasonable charges where
the assistance requested goes materially beyond that which would ordinarily be required in the course of Top Marks'
obligations under this Agreement.
7. International transfers
Top Marks shall not transfer Personal Data to any country outside the United Kingdom or the European Economic Area,
whether to a sub-processor or otherwise, unless:
(a) the destination country is the subject of regulations under section 17A of the Data Protection Act 2018 or an
adequacy decision of the European Commission, as applicable to the transfer in question; or
(b) the transfer is subject to appropriate safeguards as required by the Data Protection Legislation, including the UK
International Data Transfer Agreement or Addendum (for transfers from the UK) or the approved EU Standard
Contractual Clauses (for transfers from the EEA), such that data subjects have enforceable rights and effective legal
remedies.
8. Sub-processors
The Customer gives Top Marks general written authorisation, for the purposes of Article 28(2) of the Data Protection
Legislation, to engage the sub-processors listed at topmarks.ai/subprocessors to process Personal Data on Top Marks'
behalf in connection with the Platform, the Onboarding Services and the Support Services.
Top Marks may engage a new sub-processor to process Personal Data, or materially change the role of an existing
sub-processor, provided that Top Marks:
a) first gives the Customer not less than 30 days' written notice, identifying the sub-processor, its processing role, its
location, and the reason for the change; and

name: Top Marks AI
text:
b) maintains the list at topmarks.ai/subprocessors with version control and a change log, and notifies the Customer's
data protection contact identified in the Contract (or, if none is identified, the Customer's Administrator) of each update.
The Customer may object to a proposed change on reasonable data protection grounds by giving written notice within
20 days of receiving notice under paragraph (a) above. The parties shall discuss the objection in good faith and Top
Marks shall use reasonable endeavours to accommodate it, including by making the Platform available without the
proposed sub-processor where technically feasible.
Where the objection cannot be resolved within 30 days and Top Marks proceeds with the change, the Customer may
terminate the affected Contract by written notice, and Top Marks shall refund Fees paid in respect of the unexpired
portion of the Licence Period. Top Marks shall not permit the proposed sub-processor to process Personal Data while an
objection notified under this paragraph remains unresolved.
Where a change is required urgently to maintain the security or availability of the Platform, Top Marks may make the
change with such shorter notice as is reasonably practicable and shall notify the Customer as soon as possible
thereafter. The Customer's rights of objection and termination described above continue to apply.
9. Sub-processor contracts
Top Marks shall, before permitting any sub-processor to process Personal Data on its behalf:
(a) enter into a written contract with that sub-processor which imposes data protection obligations on that sub-processor
that are equivalent in all material respects to those imposed on Top Marks under this Schedule 1, including in particular
obligations relating to:
(i) processing Personal Data only on Top Marks' documented instructions;
(ii) implementing appropriate technical and organisational security measures in accordance with Article 32 of the Data
Protection Legislation;
(iii) maintaining confidentiality of the Personal Data;
(iv) assisting with data subject rights requests and breach notification obligations; and
(v) deleting or returning Personal Data on termination; and
(b) subject to clause 11.3, remain fully liable to the Customer for the acts and omissions of each sub-processor to the
same extent as if Top Marks had carried out the processing itself, where the sub-processor fails to fulfil its data
protection obligations under that written contract.
Top Marks shall, on written request from the Customer, confirm that the relevant written contracts are in place, and shall
make available to the Customer such information as is reasonably necessary to demonstrate that each sub-processor
processing Personal Data is bound by obligations equivalent to those set out in this Schedule 1.
10. Audit
Top Marks shall make available to the Customer all information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance with
this Schedule 1, and shall allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the Customer or an
auditor mandated by the Customer, provided that:
(a) the Customer gives at least 30 days' written notice of an audit, save where an audit is required by a supervisory
authority or follows a personal data breach affecting the Customer's Personal Data;
(b) audits take place no more than once in any 12-month period, during Business Hours, and are conducted so as to
minimise disruption to Top Marks' business and without compromising the security of other customers' data;
(c) any auditor mandated by the Customer is bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than clause 10 of
these Terms and Conditions;
(d) each party bears its own costs of the audit; and
(e) any audit or inspection of the security measures or physical data centres of Top Marks' sub-processors is limited to
Top Marks requesting and providing the audit reports or certifications produced by those sub-processors' independent
third-party auditors.
11. Return and deletion of Personal Data

name: Top Marks AI
text:
When Top Marks ceases to provide services relating to the processing of Personal Data pursuant to the Agreement (the
date on which it does so, or the date of expiry or termination of the Agreement if earlier, being the "Termination Date"),
Top Marks shall:
a) at the Customer's option (and provided that the Customer notifies Top Marks of such option within 60 days of the
Termination Date), delete or return to the Customer, or return and then delete, all Personal Data in Top Marks'
possession or control that relates to the Agreement, and Top Marks shall comply with any such request within 30 days of
the applicable request. Personal Data returned under this paragraph 11(a) shall be provided in a commonly used,
machine-readable format, and Top Marks shall confirm to the Customer in writing when the request has been given
effect;
b) whether or not a request is made under paragraph 11(a), promptly and in any event by the later of (i) 90 days after the
Termination Date and (ii), where the Customer has requested return under paragraph 11(a), 30 days after Top Marks
has completed that return, delete all copies of the Personal Data in Top Marks' possession or control that relates to the
Agreement. Limb (ii) extends the period in limb (i) only to the extent necessary to complete a return requested under
paragraph 11(a), and in no event beyond 120 days after the Termination Date;
c) not commence deletion under paragraph 11(b) before expiry of the export period set out in clause 13.4(e) of these
Terms and Conditions, save where the Customer has requested earlier deletion under paragraph 11(a);
d) hold any Personal Data which Top Marks is required by Applicable Law to retain notwithstanding paragraphs 11(a)
and 11(b) in segregated form, process it for no purpose other than that required by Applicable Law, and delete it as soon
as that requirement ceases to apply. Top Marks shall, on the Customer's written request, identify the categories of
Personal Data retained under this paragraph 11(d) and the legal requirement relied upon; and
e) notwithstanding paragraphs 11(a) and 11(b), where Personal Data persists in encrypted backup media after deletion
from Top Marks' live systems, Top Marks shall not be required to delete that Personal Data from such media otherwise
than in accordance with its standard backup rotation cycle, provided that, for so long as such Personal Data persists,
Top Marks shall:
(i) isolate it from all processing other than that necessary to maintain the integrity and availability of the backup media
themselves;
(ii) maintain it in encrypted form and protect it against access, restoration to live systems, or disclosure; and
(iii) delete it on expiry of that rotation cycle.
Top Marks shall, on the Customer's written request, confirm the date by which Personal Data relating to the Agreement
will have been deleted from all backup media.
12. Customer warranty
The Customer warrants that it has, and will maintain, one or more valid lawful bases under the Data Protection
Legislation for the processing of the Personal Data by Top Marks and its sub-processors in accordance with the
Agreement, so that such processing complies with the Data Protection Legislation, and that it has provided, or will
provide, to data subjects (including Students and, where appropriate, their parents or guardians) all privacy information
required by Articles 13 and 14 of the UK GDPR and, where applicable, the EU GDPR, including any consents required
by Applicable Law where the Customer relies on consent.
ANNEX A — PROCESSING PARTICULARS
This Annex forms part of Schedule 1 and sets out the processing particulars required by Article 28(3) of the UK GDPR.
Capitalised terms used in this Annex have the meanings given to them in the Agreement and in Schedule 1.
1. Subject Matter of Processing
The subject matter of the processing is the provision by Top Marks of an AI-assisted automated essay and examination
marking, transcription and feedback platform (the "Platform") to the Customer, as further described in the Contract and in
clause 6.1 of the Terms and Conditions.
2. Duration of Processing
Top Marks will process Personal Data for the duration of the Licence Period set out in the applicable Contract, and
thereafter:

name: Top Marks AI
text:
(a) for such period as is necessary to fulfil any deletion or return obligation under paragraph 11 of Schedule 1, in
accordance with the timeframes set out in that paragraph; and
(b) for such further period as Top Marks is required by Applicable Law to retain any Personal Data, notwithstanding the
termination or expiry of the Agreement.
3. Nature and Purpose of the Processing
3.1 Nature of processing
The processing activities carried out by Top Marks on behalf of the Customer include:
(a) collection of student and staff data, either uploaded directly by the Customer (including via CSV upload or manual
entry) or retrieved from the Customer's Management Information System (MIS) via an API integration provided by
Wonde Ltd, at the Customer's instruction and on the Customer's authorisation;
(b) collection and ingestion of assessment materials uploaded to the Platform by the Customer or its Authorised Users,
including scanned handwritten scripts, word-processed documents, and plain text submissions;
(c) automated transcription of handwritten content by an optical character recognition (OCR) model operated by Top
Marks on cloud infrastructure under its own control (Google Cloud Platform, London, United Kingdom), during which any
incidental personal identifiers appearing in a script are processed only on that infrastructure;
(d) anonymisation of essay and assessment content, whereby student identity is separated from assessment content
through an anonymising identification system and any incidental identifiers in the transcribed content are removed, in
each case before any content is transmitted to a third-party AI model provider;
(e) automated marking and feedback generation, whereby anonymised assessment content is processed through
third-party large language model providers, accessed via an AI gateway, to generate numeric grades and written
feedback;
(f) quality control processing, including cross-checking of model outputs for consistency and accuracy and AI-generated
text detection, in each case on anonymised content;
(g) grade standardisation, whereby raw numeric outputs are processed through proprietary algorithms on Top Marks'
own servers to align with standardisation materials and correct for known LLM marking variations;
(h) generation of whole-class feedback and insights through aggregated processing of anonymised assessment content
and individual feedback;
(i) storage of assessment materials, grades, feedback, and associated metadata within the Platform database;
(j) provision of access to marking results and feedback to Authorised Users via the Platform interface;
(k) processing of data subject rights requests and breach notifications in accordance with paragraphs 4 to 6 of Schedule
1; and
(l) secure deletion or return of Personal Data upon termination of the Agreement in accordance with paragraph 11 of
Schedule 1.
3.2 Purpose of processing
Top Marks processes Personal Data solely for the following purposes:
(a) the primary purpose of providing automated marking, transcription, and feedback services to the Customer in
accordance with the Agreement;
(b) enabling the Customer and its Authorised Users to access, review, and export marking results and feedback through
the Platform;
(c) facilitating the Customer's compliance with its obligations as data controller, including in relation to data subject rights
requests;
(d) carrying out support, troubleshooting, and maintenance activities strictly as required to maintain Platform availability
and performance, limited to a small number of authorised Top Marks personnel (identified by role in the DPIA Support
Pack) and only where necessary for that purpose; and

name: Top Marks AI
text:
(e) complying with Applicable Law and the lawful and binding orders of governmental or regulatory bodies.
For the avoidance of doubt, Top Marks shall not process Personal Data for any other purpose, including for the training,
fine-tuning, or improvement of AI models or the Platform, without the explicit prior written permission of the Customer in
accordance with clause 5.2 of the Terms and Conditions.
4. Types of Personal Data Processed
Top Marks processes the following types of Personal Data on behalf of the Customer:
4.1 Student Data
(a) Full name and/or student identification number (as determined by the Customer's configuration);
(b) Class, year group, or cohort information (where explicitly provided by the Customer);
(c) Examination and essay responses, including handwritten responses converted to text through the transcription
process; and
(d) Assessment results and AI-generated feedback produced by the Platform.
The data at (a) to (d) above may be provided directly by the Customer or retrieved via the MIS integration described in
paragraph 3.1(a) of this Annex.
4.2 Staff and Administrator Data
(a) Full name;
(b) Email address;
(c) Institution name;
(d) Account identifiers and login credentials (hashed);
(e) Teacher-assessment associations (records linking uploaded assessments to individual teacher accounts); and
(f) Support and other communications between the Customer's staff and Top Marks.
4.3 Technical and Usage Data
(a) IP addresses and device identifiers;
(b) Browser type and operating system;
(c) Platform usage data, including pages visited, features used, and time spent on the Platform;
(d) Submission timestamps and upload metadata; and
(e) Authentication and access logs.
4.4 Metadata
(a) Barcode/QR code identifiers used to link anonymised assessment content to student identity records held on Top
Marks' servers;
(b) Subject and course information as provided by the Customer during the upload process; and
(c) Standardisation and marking scheme references associated with uploaded assessments.
Top Marks does not require or deliberately collect special category personal data (as defined in Article 9 UK GDPR) or
criminal convictions data (as defined in Article 10 UK GDPR) as part of its standard Services. Where the Customer
believes that any assessment content may incidentally contain special category data, it should notify Top Marks prior to
upload. Free-text responses may incidentally contain Article 9 data, which is processed only as part of the assessment
content and is not used for profiling.
5. Categories of Data Subject
The Personal Data processed under this Agreement relates to the following categories of data subject:
(a) Students — pupils and students of the Customer's school, academy, or educational institution, who may include
individuals under the age of 18 and, in some cases, individuals under the age of 13. The Customer's warranty as to

name: Top Marks AI
text:
lawful basis and privacy notices is set out in paragraph 12 of Schedule 1;
(b) Teaching Staff and Authorised Users — teachers, examiners, and other educational professionals employed or
engaged by the Customer who upload assessment materials and access marking results through the Platform; and
(c) School Administrators — administrative staff of the Customer who hold accounts on the Platform for the purposes of
user management and platform configuration.
6. Sub-Processors
The Customer's general written authorisation for Top Marks' use of the sub-processors listed at
topmarks.ai/subprocessors, as updated in accordance with paragraph 8 of Schedule 1, is given in paragraph 8 of
Schedule 1, and Top Marks' obligations in respect of sub-processor contracts and liability are set out in paragraph 9 of
Schedule 1.
Providers that receive only anonymised assessment content, from which personal identifiers have been removed prior to
transmission as described in paragraph 3.1(d) of this Annex (including third-party AI model providers, the AI gateway
and AI-generated text detection tools), do not process Personal Data on the Customer's behalf. They are nevertheless
listed at topmarks.ai/subprocessors for transparency.
7. International Transfers
All Personal Data processed under this Agreement is stored and processed within the United Kingdom and the
European Economic Area, on the infrastructure identified in the sub-processor list at topmarks.ai/subprocessors.
Personal Data is not transferred to any country outside the UK or the EEA in connection with the storage or processing
of Personal Data under this Agreement.
Where anonymised assessment content is transmitted to AI model providers located in the United States for the
purposes of AI marking and feedback generation, such transmission does not constitute a transfer of Personal Data, as
all personal identifiers are removed prior to transmission as described in paragraph 3.1(d) of this Annex.
Where any transfer of Personal Data outside the UK or the EEA is or becomes necessary, Top Marks shall implement
appropriate safeguards in accordance with paragraph 7 of Schedule 1, including:
(a) the UK International Data Transfer Agreement (IDTA), for transfers of Personal Data from the UK; and/or
(b) the approved EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), for transfers of Personal Data from the EEA.

入的第三方SDK等共享信息基本情况，各单项服务接入第三方SDK的情况可能有不同，如需了解具体单项服务接入第三方
SDK的详细情况，请您前往对应的服务页面并查阅我们各单项服务的具体条款和相关页面。您也可以选择通过本政策“如

如上所述服务由相关的第三方负责运营。您使用该等第三方服务（包括您向该等第三方提供的任何
个人信息），须受第三方自己的服务条款及个人信息保护声明（而非本政策）约束，您需要仔细阅

务并采取相应的安全措施。
七、未成年人保护
我们建议：任何未成年人参加网上活动应事先取得父母或其他监护人（以下简称"监护人"）的同意。

交个人信息之前，寻求其同意和指导。
八、通知和修订
为了给您提供更好的服务，我们可能根据有道服务的更新情况及法律法规的相关要求适时修改本《
隐私政策》的条款，该等修改构成本《隐私政策》的一部分。我们会在本页面上公布对本政策所作
的任何变更。对于重大变更，我们会提供更显著的通知（包括站内红点提示、网站公告、推送通知、
弹窗提示、站内信或其他方式），本政策所指的重大变更包括但不限于：
1、我们的服务模式发生重大变化。如处理个人信息的目的、处理的个人信息类型、个人信息的使用方式等； 2、我们在
所有权结构方面发生重大变化。如业务调整、破产并购等引起的所有者变更等； 3、个人信息共享、转让或公开披露的主
要对象发生重大变化； 4、您参与个人信息处理方面的权利及其行使方式发生重大变化； 5、我们负责处理个人信息安全
的责任部门、联络方式及投诉渠道发生重大变化； 6、其他重要的或可能严重影响您的个人权益的情况发生。
您如果不同意该等变更，可以选择停止使用有道服务；如您仍然继续使用有道服务的，即表示同意

我们的任何修改都会将您的满意度置于首位。我们鼓励您在每次使用有道服务时都查阅我们的隐私政策。 我们可能在必
需时（例如当我们由于系统维护而暂停某一项服务时）发出与服务有关的公告。您可能无法取消这些与服务有关、性质不
属于推广的公告。最后，您必须对您的账号和密码信息负有保密义务。任何情况下，请小心妥善保管。
九、如何联系我们
